novelty.justification: The core novelty route is a new mechanistic relationship: the claim predicts that “a shared, language-agnostic harm/permissibility representation exists” while cross-lingual inconsistency comes from “a per-language shift of a scalar refusal gate,” with the shift tracking alignment coverage rather than typological distance. Searches for “multilingual refusal direction language-specific threshold,” “cross-lingual safety activation steering shared harm representation,” and “low-resource language jailbreak alignment coverage typological distance” found multilingual behavioral safety-gap work such as Do Methods to Jailbreak and Defend LLMs Generalize Across Languages? (2025), single-direction refusal work such as Arditi et al. (2024), and cross-language direction transfer in Activation Steering for Masked Diffusion Language Models (2025), but none establishes the claimed shared-harm-versus-language-set-threshold dissociation. Moving from those results to a language-conditioned threshold whose baseline is predicted by alignment coverage requires a new core causal relationship rather than merely transferring a standard refusal-direction analysis to another language, although it remains an advance within established multilingual-safety and activation-steering frameworks rather than a new paradigm.
